scores.notes: Holmes kneels on the bed facing left toward Watson and the match, swinging his cane into empty air while the bell-pull and snake are behind his back on the right wall. Additionally, the bell-pull rope emerges directly out of a wall ventilator while a second ventilator sits on the adjoining wall.

David stands by the brook placing a smooth stone into his shepherd's pouch with his staff and sling in his left hand, while Goliath and his shield-bearer stand across the valley. Anatomy, setting, and details match the verse cleanly with no lettering or artifacts.

Paul teaches and encourages a gathered room of first-century believers in warm light streaming through the doorway, fitting the epistle passage. Figures, hands, and scrolls are coherent and free of lettering.

The card soldiers on the far left and behind Alice's legs are drawn as human men wearing playing-card tabards on their chests rather than flat, oblong cards with hands and feet at the corners, breaking the work's depiction rule. Alice's towering size, yellow dress, King, Queen, and animal jury otherwise fit the scene.

Alice, the March Hare, the sleeping Dormouse, and the Hatter sit silently at the tea table under the tree while Alice rests her chin in thought. Animal faces and dress, Alice's yellow dress, anatomy, and props follow all rules with no lettering.

While Goliath falls forward before David and his sling, three spearheads appear on the left with two identical blades aligned on opposite ends of the same diagonal shaft behind Goliath's right arm, creating an incoherent double-ended spear alongside a third long spear.

The three card soldiers holding spears in the left background are drawn as human men in red sleeves and hoods wearing heart-pip tabards instead of flat, oblong cards with hands and feet at the corners, breaking the depiction rule. The Hatter biting his teacup, Queen in spectacles, March Hare and Dormouse arm-in-arm, and blank hat card and slates otherwise fit the moment.

King Hezekiah oversees scribes with blank scrolls and temple workers beside the bronze sea and Temple doors, fitting his wholehearted service to God's house and law. All scrolls are free of lettering and figures are anatomically sound.

The hoisting ropes are contradictory: two workers on the left haul on a rope that drops straight to the empty floor of the pit nowhere near Daniel, while Daniel clings to two separate unattached dangling ropes held by two other workers, and a fourth loose rope drapes over the foreground ledge.

Small unreadable lines of script/squiggles and numeral-like marks appear on the hotel-bill slip Holmes holds in the center, along with faint dial marks on the mantel clock. The staging of Lestrade protesting while Holmes examines the bill and Watson watches by the fire is otherwise accurate and coherent.

Moses holds two separate staffs at once—a tall curved shepherd's crook in his right hand and a second wooden rod in his outstretched left hand—creating a contradictory object duplication. No figure of God is drawn and the parted sea and Israelites are otherwise well-rendered.

Moses raises his rod against the rock as water pours out abundantly while Aaron stands beside him and the congregation and livestock gather to drink. Poses, anatomy, and setting are coherent and free of lettering.

The weeping Mock Turtle and the Gryphon solemnly dance around Alice on the seashore, waving their forelimbs as described. Alice's yellow dress and striped stockings avoid screen-adaptation clichés, and all three figures have clean anatomy.

Breaks the visionary-creatures rule because the two flanking seraphim have only two wings with uncovered faces and feet instead of six wings covering face and feet (and even the central seraph's feet remain uncovered). It also collages in burning coals in tongs from a later verse, duplicated symmetrically on both side angels aiming them into empty air.

Two attendants help an unharmed Daniel up the stone steps out of the den while King Darius greets him gladly and calm lions sit in the opening below. Architecture, guards, anatomy, and details are clean and coherent.

Jesus sleeps peacefully on a cushion in the stern while panicked disciples wake him, cling to the mast and rigging, and bail water in the raging storm. Boat structure, ropes, hands, and faces are all coherent.

Weary travelers along a mountain road beneath sunlit Jerusalem include a fallen man being lifted by an elder and a prophet looking toward the breaking light, fitting Isaiah 40:29 and its context. Figures and anatomy are well-formed with no lettering.

Holmes in a top hat thumps the pavement vigorously with his walking stick outside the brick pawnbroker's shop with three gilt balls in Saxe-Coburg Square while Watson watches. The signboards are kept blank without lettering, and anatomy and Victorian dress are clean.

Moses stands on a rocky promontory at night in a strong wind, holding his staff in his left hand and stretching his right hand over the divided sea as the Israelites watch. No human figure of God appears in the moonlit clouds, and all figures and livestock are coherent.

The father compassionately embraces his ragged, barefoot returning son on the dusty road with the family estate visible in the distance. All visible hands, fingers, faces, and feet are anatomically sound and match Luke 15:20.

Daniel stands unharmed inside the circular stone den speaking up to King Darius and his guards at the rim, while an angel stands beside four calm lions with shut mouths. Daniel's halo has no inscriptions, and all figures and lions are coherent.

The solemn Levite hands a cloth-wrapped parcel to a messenger across a table bearing a clean knife and five wrapped parcels while shocked Israelites look on outside the doorway. This conveys Judges 19:29 seriously without gore, with clean anatomy and no lettering.

In the vaulted brick bank cellar stacked with crates, Holmes kneels with a lantern and magnifying glass examining the flagstones while Mr. Merryweather sits glumly on a crate and Watson and Peter Jones watch. All four figures, hands, and props are coherent and match the text.

Moses gestures from a rocky overlook beside an Israelite aide as the people break camp below dark Mount Horeb and march with their flocks toward the distant sunlit plains. God is not depicted as a figure, and people and livestock are coherent.

Household members fill a vaulted stone treasury with silver vessels, coins, and grain sacks under an older householder's welcoming gaze, illustrating filled treasuries without drawing an allegorical figure of Wisdom. Architecture, hands, and vessels are clean and free of lettering.

In a torchlit courtyard, King Darius presses his signet ring into clay atop a rope-bound stone slab laid over the lions' den while three Persian lords, guards, and laborers watch. Ropes, hands, and expressions are coherent and free of lettering.

The father stands beside his ragged, barefoot returning son and directs servants who bring out an embroidered blue robe, a ring, and leather sandals. Poses, hands, feet, and garments are coherent and closely match Luke 15:22.

In the brick bank vault, Merryweather and Peter Jones crouch behind crates while Holmes closes the slide on his dark-lantern and Watson rests his cocked revolver atop a crate in the foreground. All four figures, hands, and props match the passage cleanly.

Moses raises his rod to the rock as abundant water streams out while Aaron stands beside him in priestly attire and the congregation and livestock gather with jars and cupped hands. Figures, animals, and details are clean and coherent.

The father runs down the dusty road from his distant estate to wrap his arms around his ragged, barefoot returning son and kiss his cheek. All intertwined arms, hands, and feet connect properly and match Luke 15:20.

Samuel pours oil from a horn onto kneeling young David's head amidst Jesse and David's brothers while wind stirs leaves through the air. No human figure represents the Spirit, and all faces, hands, and postures are coherent.

Paul stands with scrolls tucked in his sash speaking warmly to a gathered community of believers in a sunlit courtyard, fitting the encouraging epistle verse. All figures, hands, and courtyard details are coherent and free of lettering.

Bound Jesus flanked by guards turns to look across the nighttime courtyard fire at stricken Peter while a rooster crows atop the rear stone wall. Setting, crowd, anatomy, and action faithfully match Luke 22:61.

Golden beams of light break through dark clouds to illuminate the rolling primordial waters, depicting Genesis 1:3 directly. No human face or body of God appears in the clouds or light, and there is no lettering or frame.

While Peter takes the lame beggar by the right hand outside the golden Temple gate with John beside him, both Peter and John carry large fishing nets slung over their shoulders—objects contradictory to the Jerusalem Temple setting and prayer moment.
